apertura.texto: How wide open the hole is that lets light in. Small number (f/2.8) = wide open: lots of light comes in and the background comes out blurry. Large number (f/11) = closed down: everything comes out sharp.

compensacion.texto: An adjustment to tell the camera “make it darker” (negative numbers, like -1) or “brighter” (positive). At sunset, making it a little darker keeps the sky from blowing out.

iso.texto: Sensitivity to light. Low ISO (100) = clean photo but it needs more light or more time. High ISO (1600 or more) = lets you shoot in low light, but with more grain.

velocidad.texto: How long the sensor receives light. 1/500 s is very fast (it freezes movement); 1 s is very slow and needs a tripod.

modo-av.texto: You choose the aperture and the camera chooses the rest. It's called Av on Canon and A on Nikon and Sony. It's the easiest mode to start taking control of the photo.

modo-tv.texto: You choose the shutter speed and the camera chooses the rest. It's called Tv on Canon and S on Nikon and Sony.

modo-m.texto: You choose everything: aperture, shutter speed and ISO. It's only worth it when the light doesn't change, like with the moon at night and the camera on a tripod.

medicion.texto: How the camera decides how much light there is. “Evaluative” looks at the whole scene and works almost every time. “Spot” looks at only a small point: useful for measuring the sky next to the sun.

enfoque-manual.texto: Focusing yourself with the ring on the lens. With the moon, zoom in on the image on the screen and turn the ring until the edges and craters look sharp.

disparador.texto: A delay so the camera fires two seconds after you press the button and doesn't shake from your finger. You turn it on with the clock icon in the shooting menu.

raw.texto: A file with all the information from the sensor, meant for editing afterwards. It takes up more space and needs editing software.

jpeg.texto: The photo already processed by the camera. It takes up little space and can be shared directly.

hora-dorada.texto: The hour after sunrise and the hour before sunset, when the light is warm and soft.

hora-azul.texto: The stretch after sunset when the sky turns a deep blue before it gets completely dark.

paso-de-luz.texto: Double or half the light. One stop more is double; one stop less is half. Going from f/4 to f/2.8, from 1/60 s to 1/30 s and from ISO 200 to ISO 400 each gives one more stop of light.

parasol.texto: The piece that goes on the front of the lens, like the brim of a cap. It cuts the light that comes in from the side, so there are fewer reflections and the photo has more contrast. It doesn't help if the sun is inside the frame.

filtro-uv.texto: A clear piece of glass that screws onto the front of the lens. With film it filtered ultraviolet light; on a digital camera it is no longer needed, and today it is used mostly to protect the lens glass from dust, sand and scratches.

bloqueo-ae-af.texto: It fixes focus and exposure on the point you tapped, so they don't change even if you move the phone or the light changes. On iPhone you hold your finger on the point until you see “AE/AF Lock”; on other phones it may be a padlock or a similar notice.

zoom-digital.texto: Cropping part of the photo and enlarging it. It adds no detail: the more it is enlarged, the blurrier or more pixelated it looks. It is the same as cropping afterwards in an editor. Optical zoom, on the other hand, uses a different lens.

regla-de-tercios.texto: Imagine the photo divided into three equal parts across and down, like a three-by-three grid. Putting the subject or the horizon on one of those lines, or where they cross, usually gives a more balanced photo than putting them in the center.

enfoque-continuo.texto: A focus mode in which the camera keeps focusing while you hold the shutter button halfway, so a moving subject doesn't come out blurry. It's called AF-C on Nikon and AI Servo on Canon; each brand has its own name for it.

rafaga.texto: You hold down the shutter button and the camera takes many photos in a row, several per second. It's useful for capturing a moment that lasts an instant and then keeping the best one. On many phones you do it by holding down the shutter button.

lineas-guia.texto: Lines in the scene (a street, a railing, a shadow) that lead the eye toward the subject. Looking for them before you shoot helps the photo have direction.

histograma.texto: A graph that shows how much of a photo is dark, medium and bright: shadows on the left and highlights on the right. If everything piles up against the left, the photo is dark; against the right, it is very bright.

verticales-convergentes.texto: The vertical lines of a building that seem to lean toward each other at the top, as if the building were falling backward, when you tilt the camera to photograph it. You avoid them by keeping the camera level.

punto-de-fuga.texto: The spot in a photo where lines that are really parallel, like the edges of a road or train tracks, seem to meet. It gives a sense of depth and pulls the eye.

balance-de-blancos.texto: A setting that tells the camera the color of the light so whites come out white. Under a bulb a photo leans orange, and in the shade, blue. Auto usually corrects it well.

distancia-focal.texto: A number, in millimeters, that tells how much of the scene a lens takes in. A small number gives a wide view (wide angle); a big one, a narrow view that looks closer (telephoto). On a zoom it changes as you zoom.

filtro-nd.texto: A dark, neutral glass that goes in front of the lens and lets less light through. It lets you use long times in full light without blowing out the photo. Its strength is measured in stops of light.

enfoque-simple.texto: A focus mode where, when you half-press the shutter button, focus locks and stays put. It suits still subjects; if the subject moves, you have to focus again.
